Competition Prep[edit]

Studying for the F=ma Exam[edit]

The F=ma exam is the first-round selection exam for the US Physics team, which selects five travelers to compete in the International Physics Olympiad.

  • Problems and Solutions in Introductory Mechanics by David Morin. This is the single most-important book for F=ma training. A few of the problems require calculus (which the F=ma exam does not), but anyone who works through this entire book should be well-prepared for the test.
  • Physics by Halliday, Resnick, and Krane (see note in USAPhO section) This is a calculus-based textbook that is very thorough, and good for getting a deeper understanding. It has thousands of challenging problems and is useful for those who have covered the basics of mechanics and want to go deeper. It also covers many other topics in physics and will carry forward to the USAPhO exam.
  • F=ma 2011-2019 Problems and Solutions Manual (DRAFT)

Studying for the USAPhO, IPhO, and other physics olympiads[edit]

  • Physics by Halliday, Resnick, and Krane (see note below). This is an important book to read to prepare for the USAPhO exam. This book covers everything and contains many challenging problems.
  • Introduction to Classical Mechanics by David Morin. This book will take you deeper into mechanics, including some material (such as Lagrangian mechanics) beyond the syllabus of Olympiads.
  • Electricity and Magnetism by Edward M. Purcell and David Morin. This is a great book on electromagnetism for those who want to learn it with multidimensional and vector calculus.
  • Official IPhO problems from past Olympiads are available for download.
  • Jaan Kalda's resources contain a huge number of practice problems.

Note: Halliday and Resnick's textbook split into two versions because after their first textbook had existed for a decade, some colleges began asking for an easier version.

  • "Physics" by Resnick, Halliday, and Krane is in its 5th edition (published 2001). This book is often called "HRK". It is the recommended book for Olympiad preparation. The current editor is Paul Stanley, former academic director of the US Physics team. This edition has many challenging problems in it.
  • "Fundamentals of Physics" by Halliday, Resnick, edited by Walker is in its 12th edition (published 2021). This edition describes the basic physics of the same topics as HRK. However, it goes into less detail, omits some of the interesting calculations, and has far fewer challenging problems. Although this is a good book, it is not written to train students to anywhere close to the same level of problem-solving ability as HRK. So, HRK is recommended for those interested in improving their problem-solving ability to the level of physics competitions.

Books of Problems[edit]

  • Thinking Physics by Lewis Carroll Epstein (a book of conceptual problems for students learning physics for the first time)
  • Aptitude Test Problems in Physics by S.S. Krotov. More geared towards JEE preparation.
  • Problems and Solutions in Introductory Mechanics by David Morin (A good book for preparing to the F=ma exam and for practicing basic mechanics)
  • 200 Puzzling Physics Problems by Gnadig (USAPhO / IPhO level problems)
  • 200 More Puzzling Physics Problems by Gnadig (USAPhO / IPhO level problems)
  • 300 Creative Physics Problems with Solutions by Holics (USAPhO / IPhO level problems)
  • Physics to a Degree by Thomas and Raine (USAPhO / IPhO level problems)
  • Thinking Like a Physicist by Thompson (USAPhO / IPhO level problems)
